## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upasāḷakajātaka* (Ja 166) is a verse narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Canon. The story's traditional background, set while the Buddha was residing at the Jetavana monastery, concerns a brahmin named Upasāḷha who was exceptionally fastidious about cemeteries, prompting the Buddha to utter the verse beginning with the declaration of "fourteen thousand Upasalhas". In art-historical and epigraphical records of the Pagan period in Myanmar, ink glosses on temple murals document the canonical sequence of the Jātaka tales, noting instances where narrative depictions of Jātaka 166 (termed *Upasāļha*) were omitted [Win Than Tun 2002].

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus detects internal Pali textual reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo) and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, aligning segment ranges across §§ 1.1–3.1 [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meet the reporting threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
